sampling_model.design: Superpopulation observational sampling with no parametric model for the categorical distribution, propensities, or outcome regressions.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment \(A\) with identification by consistency and conditional exchangeability given \(X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Fixed \(\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass category.
sampling_model.outcome: Real outcomes with \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\) and explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth central moments at most \(M^4\); this implies conditional variances at most \(M^2\) but imposes no standardized-kurtosis or positive-variance condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On the balanced local class, the explicit cross-fitted saturated-cell nuisance estimators have derived weighted squared-error order \(d_n/n\), which yields the one-step orthogonal remainder \(O_P(d_n/n)\). The heavy-light handle uses the pilot rule \(\min_aN_{ak}^{(0)}\le256\log(en)\) and exactly equals the saturated one-step center and variance when every category is heavy; its radii remain proposed outputs.
sampling_model.computation: Categorical and treatment coordinates are exact and outcomes have dyadic enclosures. Polynomial and falling-factorial recurrences admit outward interval evaluation, but certified bisection is unavailable until the nonmonotone light score is replaced or confined to a bracket with a uniform positive slope and the heavy score is explicitly specified.
sampling_model.randomness: All probabilities and expectations are under the observed iid sample law \(Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 lower-bounds worst-case mean squared error for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\) by the order of \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\) under fixed overlap; Appendix C.5 sets the control-arm regression to zero in the hard family.
The paper constructs heavy-light best-polynomial factorial-moment estimators attaining minimax mean squared error for additive discrete-distribution functionals.

Sections 4.1--4.2 provide scalar bounded-influence score inequalities, but they do not prove a tail theorem for this pilot-selected marked-factorial statistic; moreover, the symmetric half-log transform stipulated here is not globally monotone and needs a retained-range theorem or score replacement before root inversion is valid.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds expected confidence length in Gaussian nonparametric experiments by a between-class modulus and the paper constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals.
Theorem 5.1 gives uniformly valid asymptotically efficient Gaussian ATE intervals from cross-fitted orthogonal scores under nuisance-rate conditions.

The Abstract and Sections 2--4 derive finite-sample optimal bias-aware ATE estimators and confidence intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions when regression errors are normal with known variance, with feasible asymptotic extensions for unknown errors.

Theorem 3.1 gives a self-normalized moderate-deviation expansion for fixed-order nondegenerate Studentized U-statistics under moment conditions; its degree-one consequence is used only for the oracle-score central limit step.
The paper gives nearly tight dimension-free confidence intervals for probabilities of individually unobserved multinomial events.

tldr: The same-class testing converse is established, and the strongest unconditional honest-length result is currently the bracket \(r_{n,d,M}\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\le4M\). This round separately proves the saturated one-step expansion, ratio-consistent variance, and Gaussian limit, proves that every pilot arm-cell is heavy with probability \(1-o(1)\) on the balanced local class, and corrects the heavy-light handle to impose the exact all-heavy center/variance override. The sharp global upper bound, certified computation, heavy-light radius limit, and endpoint equivalence remain open because neither the selected-factorial radius nor the hybrid heavy Gaussian/fallback radius is defined and certified.

project_justification.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 supplies the large-alphabet point-risk obstruction and the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) application, but not a directly calibrated honest expected-length upper bound. The accepted factorial construction supplies the light approximation bias, while the stipulated symmetric half-log score is nonmonotone and the heavy Gaussian/fallback score is absent.
project_justification.niche: The unresolved contribution is a globally honest interval for arbitrary categorical masses that also uses the efficient Gaussian radius on balanced tables. The exact all-heavy override now makes this adaptive target mathematically well posed without treating the local one-step benchmark as a substitute for it.
project_justification.fill: The core now contains a proved same-class lower bound, a closed fallback bracket, a proved saturated one-step local benchmark, and an exponential all-heavy pilot bound. Completion requires an explicit monotone selected-factorial calibration with pilot-shift control and an explicit heavy score whose high-variance branch has Gaussian critical value and whose fallback branch is finite-sample honest.

related_work: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 remains the application and point-risk anchor and supports the moment-matching architecture behind the proved same-class converse, but it does not supply the present honest upper interval. CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026 supplies the clipped real-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator and light-bias architecture, not a direct tail theorem. Catoni2012 provides scalar bounded-influence inequalities but not unique-root calibration for the redescending symmetric half-log score used here. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML and Hahn1998 are matched by the separate proved saturated one-step benchmark; they do not connect that benchmark to a finite-sample honest arbitrary-mass interval. ShaoZhou2016 supports only the already-declared degree-one self-normalized central-limit step. ArmstrongKolesar2021, CaiLow2004, and Painsky2022 remain adjacent comparators rather than sources of the missing global construction.
technical_internal_limitation: For the stipulated symmetric score, \(\psi'(x)=2(2-x^2)/(x^4+4)\), so the score is redescending, has stationary points at \(\pm\sqrt2\), and can have at least three roots. Thus monotone inversion and a uniform score-to-root error modulus are unavailable. Conditioning on the common pilot also centers block fluctuations at a pilot-dependent mean rather than the unconditional expectation. Separately, no heavy hybrid score presently combines a studentized Gaussian branch with a bounded-influence finite-sample fallback.
honest_scope: The global model still permits arbitrary and zero cell masses and imposes only fixed overlap, bounded cell means, and an absolute conditional fourth-central-moment envelope. No standardized-kurtosis, positive conditional-variance, or global balance condition is added. The established confidence-length conclusion is the lower bound together with the deterministic \([-2M,2M]\) upper bracket. The balanced mass and nondegenerate efficient-variance conditions are used only for the proved one-step benchmark and all-heavy probability lemma; finite-sample heavy-light coverage, sharp expected length, certified endpoints, and heavy-light Gaussian endpoint equivalence remain open.
interpretation: When cell masses are balanced and \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), every pilot arm-cell exceeds the heavy threshold with probability \(1-o(1)\), and the corrected heavy-light center and variance then equal the efficient saturated one-step outputs. This proves that the center can adapt locally. It does not yet justify Gaussian heavy-light endpoints: that conclusion additionally requires the unresolved hybrid radius to approach \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)/n}\).

definitions.name: banked heavy-light lift compatibility handle
definitions.construction: Instantiate the explicit clipped linear-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator from CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026, \(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), after applying it to the rescaled marks \(Y/2\) and multiplying its output by two. Rewrite its light branch through \(u_k\) as a degree-\(L_n\) element of \(\mathscr Q_{L_n}\) on dyadic slices of \(\mathcal K_{\epsilon,M}(B)\); retain its independent pilot choice \(\widehat{\mathcal L}\), fixed-multinomial falling-factorial recurrence, single independent outcome mark, zero fallbacks, and clipping, and expose the resulting light statistic as \(\widehat T_{\mathrm L}\) for direct tail calibration.

definitions.name: direct marked-factorial tail-calibration handle
definitions.construction: Use Catoni's scalar bounded-influence transform only as an algebraic score template inside independent perturbation blocks of the marked factorial lift before category aggregation. Derive the required score inequalities directly from \(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\), including cells of zero or arbitrarily small conditional variance; use observable leave-block perturbations and exponential score inversion to define \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) as the smallest radius whose two-sided score is at most \(\alpha/4\), with no cellwise union bound and no post hoc median wrapper.

definitions.name: robust heavy-light interval handle
definitions.construction:
Use the pilot fold \(I_0\) and set
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal L}
 =\left\{k:\min_{a\in\{0,1\}}N_{ak}^{(0)}
 \le256\log(en)\right\}.
\]
On the all-heavy event \(\widehat{\mathcal L}=\varnothing\), set the light
contribution and its proposed radius to zero and impose the exact identities
\[
 \widehat T_{\mathrm L}=0,
 \qquad
 (\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}},\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}})
 =(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}},\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}).
\]
On the complementary event, use the light-center output of
\(def:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}lift\text{-}handle\) and the proposed
saturated treated-control heavy center and variance with within-cell
fourth-moment truncation.  In both cases, treat \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\),
the heavy radius, and their combined output
\(\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}\in[0,2M]\) only as proposed nonnegative
sample-measurable outputs.  Their explicit score formulae, the light
selected-factorial tail certificate, and the heavy Gaussian/fallback tail
certificate are not part of this construction; they remain exactly the
obligations in \(oeq:observable\text{-}rare\text{-}tail\) and
\(thm:global\text{-}honest\text{-}upper\).  Return
\[
 \widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}
 = [\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}},
    \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}+\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}]
   \cap[-2M,2M].
\]

definitions.name: certified rational implementation of the heavy-light interval
definitions.construction: Given \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\) satisfying \(2^{-b}M\le\delta_{\mathrm{num}}/[64n(en)^{8L_n}]\), use \(b_{\mathrm{work}}\) working bits. Generate shifted-Chebyshev coefficient enclosures by the three-term recurrence and interval Clenshaw evaluation; generate every factorial monomial by \((N)_0=1\) and \((N)_{\ell+1}=(N)_\ell(N-\ell)\), followed by multiplication by its single outcome-mark enclosure; evaluate bounded-influence and exponential scores using outward dyadic interval arithmetic; invert each monotone two-sided score by bisection on \([0,2M]\) until its bracket has width at most \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}/8\). Enlarge the exact-real endpoints from \(def:robust-heavy-light-interval-handle\) by the resulting certified arithmetic-error bounds and intersect with \([-2M,2M]\) to return \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\).

statements.statement: Apply CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026, \(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), to the marks \(Y/2\) and multiply its clipped output by two. For \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), the resulting banked real-mark heavy-light estimator admits the four-coordinate representation in \(def:four-coordinate-lift-handle\), is computable using \(O(dL_n^3)\) arithmetic operations, and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\widehat T_{\mathrm L}-\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})]|\lesssim_{\epsilon}Md/[n\log(en)]\); its pilot misclassification contribution has the same order. The representation preserves the banked factorial coefficients, zero fallbacks, clipping, and expectation identities and exposes the selected marked-factorial statistic required by \(def:direct-calibration-handle\).
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(L=\log(en)\) and \(\widetilde Y=Y/2\).  We invoke the established
construction
\(\mathtt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_heterogeneity\_frontier/
thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution}\) only for
its explicit clipped Chebyshev factorial estimator and its proved pilot and
approximation certificates.  Its hypotheses hold after this rescaling.  In
fact, the cell-mean envelope gives
\[
 \left|E_P[\widetilde Y\mid A=a,X=k]\right|
 =\frac{|\mu_{ak}|}{2}\le \frac M2.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover, Cauchy--Schwarz and the conditional fourth-moment condition in the
definition of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\) give
\[
 \begin{split}
 E_P\!\left[\left(\widetilde Y-\frac{\mu_{ak}}2\right)^2
       \middle|A=a,X=k\right]
 &\le
 \left\{E_P\!\left[\left(\widetilde Y-\frac{\mu_{ak}}2\right)^4
       \middle|A=a,X=k\right]\right\}^{1/2}\\
 &=\frac14
 \left\{E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid A=a,X=k]\right\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac{M^2}{4}.
 \end{split}
\tag{2}
\]
The fixed-overlap hypothesis is unchanged by rescaling, and independence of
the pilot and estimation folds follows from iid sampling.  Thus the cited
construction may be applied to \(\widetilde Y\), after which its output is
multiplied by two.

We next verify, rather than assume, the asserted four-coordinate form.  For a
cell \(k\), write
\[
 x_0=p_k(1-\pi_k),\qquad x_1=p_k\pi_k,\qquad
 z_a=x_a\mu_{ak},\qquad p_k=x_0+x_1.
\tag{3}
\]
The cited construction uses constants
\[
 K=\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor,\qquad
 \alpha_0=\min\left\{1,(64\log6)^{-1},(512D_6)^{-1}\right\},
 \qquad D_6=8\log(27/4),
\tag{4}
\]
the light-mass scale \(B=4096L/m_1\), where \(m_1\asymp n\) is the
estimation-fold size, and pilot threshold \(256L\).  Select the numerical
coefficient in \(L_n\) so that \(c_L\ge\alpha_0\); then \(K\le L_n\).
For the Chebyshev polynomial \(T_K\), define the polynomials, with their
continuous values at zero,
\[
 H_K(t)=\frac{1-T_K(1-2t)}{2K^2},\qquad
 E_K(t)=\frac{H_K(t)}t,\qquad
 G_K(t)=\frac{1-E_K(t)}t.
\tag{5}
\]
The identities \(T_K(1)=1\) and \(T'_K(1)=K^2\) show that both divisions in
(5) are exact polynomial divisions.  Since
\(T_K(\cos\vartheta)=\cos(K\vartheta)\), for \(0\le t\le1\),
\[
 0\le t\{1-tG_K(t)\}=H_K(t)\le K^{-2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Also, \(G_K\) has degree at most \(K-2\).  Hence
\[
 q_a(x_0,x_1)=\frac{x_0+x_1}{B}G_K(x_a/B)
\tag{7}
\]
has total degree at most \(K-1\le L_n-1\), and therefore
\[
 (x_0,z_0,x_1,z_1)\longmapsto
 z_1q_1(x_0,x_1)-z_0q_0(x_0,x_1)
 \in\mathscr Q_{L_n}.
\tag{8}
\]
This is the required four-coordinate rewrite on every dyadic slice of
\(\mathcal K_{\epsilon,M}(B)\).

Let \(\mathcal A\) be the pilot-good event from the cited construction.  On
\(\mathcal A\), every pilot-selected light cell obeys \(p_k\le B/4\).
For such a cell, fixed overlap yields \(x_a\ge\epsilon p_k\), while
\(0\le x_a/B\le1\).  Equations (3), (6), and the cell-mean envelope imply
\[
 \begin{split}
 \left|p_k\mu_{ak}-\frac{p_kz_a}{B}G_K(x_a/B)\right|
 &=p_k|\mu_{ak}|\frac{H_K(x_a/B)}{x_a/B}\\
 &\le \frac{MB}{\epsilon K^2}.
 \end{split}
\tag{9}
\]
Condition on the pilot sample.  An ordered distinct-index falling-factorial
term with one outcome mark is unbiased for the corresponding monomial
\(z_ap_kx_a^j\): after expansion over distinct indices, independence makes
its expectation the product of the one-observation mass and mark moments.
Linearity of this identity, first conditionally on the pilot and then
unconditionally, and summation of (9) over the two arms and at most \(d\)
selected cells give
\[
 \left|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
 \widehat T_{\mathrm L}
 -\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}
 p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\right]\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A}\right|
 \le \frac{2MdB}{\epsilon K^2}.
\tag{10}
\]
The cited pilot certificate, applied under fixed overlap and
\(d\le c_\epsilon nL\), states after decreasing \(c_\epsilon\) if necessary
that
\[
 Q_P^{(n)}(\mathcal A^c)
 \le2d\exp(-c_\epsilon256L)\le C_\epsilon n^{-6}.
\tag{11}
\]
Both the factorial output and its target contribution are clipped at the
source envelope, so (11) contributes at most \(C_\epsilon Mn^{-6}\) to
(10).  The same calculation is precisely the cited pilot-misclassification
bound.  Since \(B\asymp L/n\), \(K\asymp L\), and \(L\ge1\), (10)--(11)
yield, after enlarging the constant for the finitely many rows for which
\(K<2\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 \left|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
 \widehat T_{\mathrm L}
 -\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}
 p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\right]\right|
 \le C_\epsilon M\frac{d}{n\log(en)}.
\tag{12}
\]
Finally, the Chebyshev recurrence has \(O(L_n^2)\) coefficients per cell;
the fixed four-coordinate bookkeeping, falling-factorial recurrence, zero
fallbacks, and clipping therefore require \(O(dL_n^2)\), hence
\(O(dL_n^3)\), arithmetic operations.  Rescaling the single mark by one half
and multiplying the final output by two preserves every expectation identity,
zero fallback, clipping rule, and pilot certificate.  This proves all parts
of the lemma.
statements.justification: This compatibility lemma imports the established real-mark heavy-light approximation and verifies exactly the representation needed by the new observable tail score; it is not an independent approximation novelty claim.
statements.gap: CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026, \(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), already supplies the clipped real-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator and its risk order. The remaining bridge is to expose its pilot-selected light statistic in a form on which the data-only tail calibration can act without changing the banked expectation and bias guarantees.
statements.consumer: The bias half of the globally honest upper interval and the rare-cell contribution in the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) analysis.

statements.statement: Using \(def:direct-calibration-handle\), determine the robust perturbation blocks, bounded-influence score, polynomial constants, and score-inversion critical value for which \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) is measurable from \(\mathcal D_n\) and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{|\widehat T_{\mathrm L}-E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\widehat T_{\mathrm L}|>\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\}\le\alpha/4\) together with \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\widehat R_{\mathrm L}]\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}M\{n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\). For every valid \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\), the coefficient recurrence, factorial recurrence, outward score evaluation, and bisection in \(def:certified-finite-precision-algorithm\) must return a certified approximation to \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) with absolute error at most \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}/4\). The tail certificate must concern the selected marked-factorial statistic itself rather than a Markov conversion of its mean squared error, a cellwise union bound, or a generic median-of-means wrapper.
statements.justification: This remains the central finite-sample inference obstruction for the selected marked-factorial statistic.
statements.gap: The symmetric half-log score is nonmonotone and pilot-conditional centering does not control the unconditional target center.
statements.consumer: A deployable rare-cell coverage certificate for saturated adjustment remains the intended consumer.

obligation.what_is_open: An explicit data-measurable rare-cell score interval with a direct tail event, sharp expected radius, pilot-centering control, and certified root inversion for the selected marked-factorial statistic.
obligation.obstruction: The stipulated symmetric half-log score is redescending, has zero derivative at \(\pm\sqrt2\), and can have multiple roots. The core also lacks a score controlling the random shift between the pilot-conditional and unconditional centers.
obligation.attempted: The exact derivative and a one-remote-block configuration were analyzed before any moment-generating-function step; they disprove monotone unique-root inversion for the proposed score. The banked bias result does not supply the missing tail or pilot-shift certificate.
obligation.partial_result:
The established node \(lem:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}bias\) supplies the
bias \(C_\epsilon Md/[n\log(en)]\).  The stipulated score does not yet turn
this fact into the requested observable tail radius.  Indeed, for
\[
 \psi(x)=\frac12\log\frac{1+x+x^2/2}{1-x+x^2/2}
\]
one has
\[
 \psi'(x)=\frac{2(2-x^2)}{x^4+4}.
\]
Thus the score is increasing only on \((-\sqrt2,\sqrt2)\) and is decreasing
outside that interval.  For any odd block count \(B\ge3\), any \(\lambda>0\),
and block outputs \(Z_1=\cdots=Z_{B-1}=0\), \(Z_B=R/\lambda\), the proposed
score is
\[
 S_R(t)=-(B-1)\psi(\lambda t)+\psi(R-\lambda t).
\]
For sufficiently large \(R\), continuity and
\(\psi(x)\downarrow0\) as \(x\to\infty\) give
\[
 S_R(0)>0,\quad S_R(\sqrt2/\lambda)<0,\quad
 S_R((R-\sqrt2)/\lambda)>0,\quad S_R(R/\lambda)<0.
\]
Hence the zero equation has at least three roots.  A retained-range argument
could repair uniqueness, but no such range, positive slope modulus, or
pilot-centering correction is currently defined.

statements.statement: There is an interval specified by \(def:robust-heavy-light-interval-handle\) such that, for every \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{\tau(P)\in\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\). The guarantee uses only the observed sample, the known values \(M\), \(\epsilon\), and \(\alpha\), and the conditions defining \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).
statements.justification: The corrected handle exposes the intended sample split and all-heavy identity but does not claim unproved radii.
statements.gap: Both the selected-factorial light radius and the winsorized Gaussian/fallback heavy radius lack explicit valid sample maps and tail theorems.
statements.consumer: The intended consumer is a uniformly valid replacement for the reference intervals in the Zeng et al. 401(k) analysis.

obligation.what_is_open: Finite-sample coverage and the sharp expected-radius bound for an explicit heavy--light interval on the unrestricted global class.
obligation.obstruction: The selected-factorial rare radius remains unresolved in the sibling-owned rare-tail question, and the heavy winsorized Gaussian/fallback radius is still not an explicit sample map. The exact all-heavy center and variance override does not furnish either tail certificate.
obligation.attempted: I combined the proved light-branch bias with the exact all-heavy override and decomposed the remaining error into light fluctuation, heavy fluctuation, truncation, and pilot terms. Only the deterministic light bias and the local all-heavy bridge follow from the frozen primitives.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved light-approximation lemma supplies
\[
 \left|E\widehat T_{\mathrm L}
 -E\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}
 p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\right|
 \le C_\epsilon M\frac{d}{n\log(en)}.
\]
The frozen heavy--light handle also gives an exact center and variance
identity on the all-heavy pilot event.  If explicit light and heavy radii
satisfied their allocated conditional tail bounds and had expected sizes
\(C_{\epsilon,\alpha}M\{n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\) and
\(C_{\epsilon,\alpha}Mn^{-1/2}\), respectively, the triangle inequality and
the allocation of the noncoverage probability would prove the target, and
intersection with \([-2M,2M]\) would not enlarge length.  The frozen core
does not define radii with those properties, so this implication cannot be
turned into a proof of the stated interval theorem.

statements.statement: For every valid input \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\) with \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\le r_{n,d,M}\), \(def:certified-finite-precision-algorithm\) returns \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\) satisfying \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\subseteq\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\) and moving each endpoint outward by at most \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\). Its bit-operation count is \(O\bigl([dL_n^3+(n+d)L_n^2\lceil\log_2(8M/\delta_{\mathrm{num}})\rceil]b_{\mathrm{work}}^2\bigr)\), hence polynomial in \(\mathsf L_{\mathrm{in}}\) and \(\log(1/\delta_{\mathrm{num}})\). Consequently, its coverage is at least \(1-\alpha\) and its worst expected length is at most \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]+2\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\).
statements.justification: Outward arithmetic preserves coverage only after valid exact-real roots and an error-to-root modulus exist.
statements.gap: Nonmonotonicity, zero derivative, and the absent heavy score prevent certified bisection and the asserted bit bound.
statements.consumer: The intended consumer remains an auditable implementation for the \(n=9915,d=8196\) application.

obligation.what_is_open: A certified outward enclosure of the actual statistical score roots and the asserted bit complexity.
obligation.obstruction: No valid exact-real heavy score is defined, and the proposed light-score handle supplies neither a proved monotone inversion equation nor a positive root-slope modulus. Therefore outward score evaluation cannot be converted uniformly into endpoint accuracy.
obligation.attempted: I propagated the coefficient and factorial magnitude bounds through the declared working-precision envelope and verified deterministic interval inclusion and length inflation. The root-enclosure induction stops at the absent monotonicity and slope certificate.
obligation.partial_result:
Let the exact-real interval be \([L,U]\).  If outward interval arithmetic
returns \(\widetilde L\le L\le U\le\widetilde U\) with
\(L-\widetilde L\le\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\) and
\(\widetilde U-U\le\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\), then deterministically
\[
 [L,U]\subseteq[\widetilde L,\widetilde U],\qquad
 (\widetilde U-\widetilde L)-(U-L)\le2\delta_{\mathrm{num}}.
\]
Thus coverage is monotone under the certified enlargement.  The banked
coefficient bound and the declared working precision control the arithmetic
magnitudes of the Chebyshev and factorial recurrences.  What is unavailable
is a defined monotone statistical score with a positive root-slope modulus;
without it, score-enclosure error cannot be converted into the asserted
endpoint error or bisection count.

statements.statement: On \(\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\), \(\tau(P)=\psi_1(P)\) because \(\mu_{0k}=0\) on every positive-mass cell. More explicitly, take the control-arm-zero binary hard family used in ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, leave its zero control outcome fixed, and multiply its binary treated outcome by \(M\). The induced full-data laws belong to \(\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\subseteq\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\), preserve cell masses and propensities, satisfy the fourth-central-moment envelope, and multiply both \(\psi_1\)-separation and ATE separation by \(M\). Consequently the theorem's one-arm mean-squared-error lower scale \(M^2\{n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\) transfers by subclass restriction to ATE point estimation for \(d\lesssim_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\). Its priors may be used in \(thm:same-class-testing-converse\) only after that theorem separately proves ATE target-set separation and prior-predictive total-variation control.
statements.justification: The source result concerns the treated-arm functional, so an explicit control-zero embedding is required before its rate can inform any ATE lower-bound argument.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, lower-bound \(\psi_1\) and use a control-arm-zero proof family; the proposition records the exact subclass and scaling identity that transfer this source experiment to the ATE model without relabeling the published estimand.
statements.consumer: The rare-cell source priors for the direct same-class confidence-length converse.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  By
\(\texttt{def:control-arm-zero-binary-subclass}\), this law belongs to
\(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\), satisfies
\(Y(0)=0\) almost surely by
\(\texttt{ass:control-arm-zero-subclass}\), and satisfies
\(Y(1)\in\{0,M\}\) almost surely by
\(\texttt{ass:treated-binary-subclass}\).  If \(p_k>0\), then
\(\texttt{ass:fixed-overlap}\) gives
\[
 P(A=0,X=k)=p_k(1-\pi_k)\ge \epsilon p_k>0.
\tag{1}
\]
On \(\{A=0\}\), consistency
\(\texttt{ass:consistency}\) and \(Y(0)=0\) give \(Y=Y(0)=0\)
almost surely.  The conditional mean is therefore well defined on the event
in (1), and
\[
 \mu_{0k}=E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]=0.
\tag{2}
\]
Substituting (2) into the identifying equality in
\(\texttt{def:ate-functional}\), and then using
\(\texttt{def:one-arm-functional}\), yields
\[
 \tau(P)
 =\sum_{k=1}^d p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
 =\sum_{k=1}^d p_k\mu_{1k}
 =\psi_1(P).
\tag{3}
\]

We next verify the claimed embedding and its risk scaling.  Consider any
unit-scale law in the binary one-arm hard family to which the cited result
\(\texttt{lem:zeng-one-arm-lower}\) applies.  Write its cell masses and
propensities as \(p_k\) and \(\pi_k\), and write
\(m_k\in[0,1]\) for the success probability of its binary treated outcome
\(B\in\{0,1\}\) in cell \(k\).  Construct a full-data law
\(P^{(M)}\) as follows.  Retain the law of \(X\), draw
\(A\mid X=k\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_k)\), draw
\(B\mid X=k\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(m_k)\) independently of \(A\)
conditional on \(X\), and set
\[
 Y(0)=0,\qquad Y(1)=MB,
 \qquad Y=Y(A).
\tag{4}
\]
Thus (4) gives consistency, while the stipulated conditional independence
gives \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X\), as required by
\(\texttt{ass:conditional-exchangeability}\).  Cell masses and propensities
are unchanged, so the source family's overlap bounds imply
\(\texttt{ass:fixed-overlap}\).  For every positive-mass cell,
\[
 \mu_{0k}=0,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1k}=Mm_k,
 \qquad
 |\mu_{ak}|\le M,
\tag{5}
\]
which verifies \(\texttt{ass:cell-mean-envelope}\).  For the control arm the
conditional fourth central moment is zero.  For the treated arm, conditional
independence in (4) and \(|B-m_k|\le1\) imply
\[
 E_{P^{(M)}}[(Y-\mu_{1k})^4\mid X=k,A=1]
 =M^4E[(B-m_k)^4\mid X=k]
 \le M^4.
\tag{6}
\]
Hence \(\texttt{ass:conditional-fourth-moment}\) also holds.  Equations
(4)--(6), together with \(\texttt{def:global-law-class}\) and
\(\texttt{def:control-arm-zero-binary-subclass}\), prove
\[
 P^{(M)}\in
 \mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}.
\tag{7}
\]
Moreover, (3) and (5) give the exact target scaling
\[
 \tau(P^{(M)})
 =M\sum_{k=1}^d p_km_k
 =M\psi_1(P^{(1)}),
\tag{8}
\]
where \(P^{(1)}\) denotes the corresponding unit-scale one-arm law.  Thus
every separation between two source values of \(\psi_1\) is multiplied by
\(M\) after embedding.

For completeness, let \(T_M\) be the deterministic sample transformation
that replaces each unit-scale observed binary outcome by its product with
\(M\), leaving \(X\) and \(A\) unchanged.  By (4), applying \(T_M\) to an
iid observed sample with law \(Q_{P^{(1)}}^{(n)}\) has exactly the observed
sample law
\(Q_{P^{(M)}}^{(n)}\).  Given any measurable ATE estimator
\(\widehat\tau\), define on the source experiment
\[
 \widehat\psi(D)=M^{-1}\widehat\tau(T_M D).
\tag{9}
\]
The division in (9) is valid because \(M\ge1\).  From (8)--(9), for every
source law,
\[
 E_{Q_{P^{(1)}}^{(n)}}[(\widehat\psi-\psi_1(P^{(1)}))^2]
 =M^{-2}E_{Q_{P^{(M)}}^{(n)}}
   [\{\widehat\tau-\tau(P^{(M)})\}^2].
\tag{10}
\]
The estimator in (9) is an admissible estimator in the source experiment.
Therefore \(\texttt{lem:zeng-one-arm-lower}\), followed by (7) and (10),
implies for every \(\widehat\tau\)
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\}^2]
 &\ge
 \sup_{P^{(1)}\ \mathrm{in\ the\ source\ hard\ family}}
 E_{Q_{P^{(M)}}^{(n)}}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\tau(P^{(M)})\}^2]\\
 &\ge c_{\epsilon}M^2
 \left\{n^{-1}+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}
 \end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
throughout the dimension range stated by that cited lemma.  Taking the
infimum of (11) over all measurable \(\widehat\tau\) establishes the claimed
ATE point-estimation lower scale by subclass restriction.

Finally, (11) is only a minimax squared-error statement.  Its derivation does
not assert that the source lower-bound prior puts its ATE values in two
separated target sets after any conditioning, nor does it bound total
variation between the corresponding prior-predictive observed laws.  Those
are distinct hypotheses of the interval testing argument in
\(\texttt{lem:coverage-testing-inequality}\).  Accordingly, this proposition
does not by itself imply a confidence-length lower bound; the direct
target-set separation and prior-predictive total-variation calculation used
for that purpose are supplied separately in
\(\texttt{thm:same-class-testing-converse}\), exactly as the final sentence
of the proposition states.

statements.statement: Let \(C_n\) be any interval satisfying the coverage constraint in \(def:minimax-honest-length\). For every pair \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) and target sets \(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1\) satisfying \(def:prior-predictive-pair\), \(E_{\mathbb Q_0}[|C_n|]\ge\Delta(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1)\{1-2\alpha-\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}_+\).
statements.justification: Uniform coverage forces a long interval whenever the observed experiments are close but their ATE sets are separated.
statements.gap: Low1997 and CaiLow2004, Theorem 1, establish coverage-to-length inequalities in nonparametric Gaussian models; this lemma states the experiment-level version needed for prior mixtures in the discrete causal model.
statements.consumer: The direct confidence-length converse, without reducing interval performance to squared-error risk.
statements.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 A_j:=\{C_n\cap\mathcal T_j\ne\varnothing\},\qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Uniform coverage and the support condition in
\(def:prior\text{-}predictive\text{-}pair\) imply
\[
 \mathbb Q_j(A_j)
 \ge\int Q_P^{(n)}\{\tau(P)\in C_n\}\,d\Pi_j(P)
 \ge1-\alpha.
\tag{1}
\]
By the defining variational inequality for total variation,
\[
 \mathbb Q_0(A_1)\ge \mathbb Q_1(A_1)
 -\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \ge1-\alpha-\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\tag{2}
\]
The union bound applied under \(\mathbb Q_0\) to (1)--(2) gives
\[
 \mathbb Q_0(A_0\cap A_1)
 \ge1-2\alpha-\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\tag{3}
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the interval \(C_n\) contains a point of each target
set.  Because it is an interval, its length is at least
\(\Delta(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1)\).  Multiplying this deterministic
inequality by \(\mathbf1_{A_0\cap A_1}\), taking \(\mathbb Q_0\)-expectations,
and replacing the right side of (3) by its positive part proves the claim.

statements.statement:
For every \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\),
\[
 \mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}
 \gtrsim_{\epsilon,\alpha} r_{n,d,M}.
\]
The \(Mn^{-1/2}\) component is certified by two point-mass priors supported on the exact fixed-\(n\) class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  The rare-cell component is certified without asserting an unsupported exact fixed-\(n\) rare-prior pair: at Poisson intensity \(N=4n\), condition the published moment-matching priors on simultaneous mass and one-arm-functional concentration, use their directly computed count-mixture total-variation bound, and map every exact-\(n\) honest interval into that relaxed experiment by uniformly selecting \(n\) observations when the Poisson total is at least \(n\), applying the interval to the normalized law, and enlarging it by the observable-independent mass-defect allowance \(M\delta\).  This gives the rare-cell lower bound \(M d/[n\log(en)]\) when \(d\gtrsim_{\epsilon}\log^4(en)\); in the complementary regime that term is bounded by a constant multiple of \(Mn^{-1/2}\).  Thus the displayed full-width frontier is a direct consequence of uniform same-class coverage and a confidence-interval de-Poissonization argument, not of taking the square root of a point-estimation risk bound.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the proposed statement.  Throughout, total variation is normalized to lie in \([0,1]\).

First let \(C_n\) be any interval admissible in \(\texttt{def:minimax-honest-length}\).  The exact-class point-mass priors from \(\texttt{lem:root-n-testing-priors}\), followed by \(\texttt{lem:coverage-testing-inequality}\), give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|C_n|]
 \ge \kappa_\alpha M n^{-1/2},
\tag{1}
\]
where
\[
 \kappa_\alpha
 =(1-2\alpha)
 \min\!\left\{\frac14,
 \sqrt{\frac{3\log\{1+(1-2\alpha)^2\}}{32}}\right\}>0.
\]
Indeed, the target separation in that lemma is twice the displayed minimum times \(Mn^{-1/2}\), while its total-variation upper bound is \((1-2\alpha)/2\).  Taking the infimum over admissible \(C_n\) proves
\[
 \mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}
 \ge \kappa_\alpha M n^{-1/2}.
\tag{2}
\]

We next prove the rare-cell bound by a confidence-interval de-Poissonization.  Put
\[
 N=4n,\qquad D=d-1.
\tag{3}
\]
Only the regime \(D\ge A\log^4N\) and \(N\ge N_0\), for constants \(A,N_0\) fixed below, needs a rare-cell construction.  In particular \(D\ge1\).  Since \(d\le c_\epsilon n\log(en)\), \(c_\epsilon\le1\), and \(N=4n\),
\[
 D\le N\log N.
\tag{4}
\]

Apply \(\texttt{lem:zeng-moment-matching-triples}\) with sample-size argument \(N\), dimension argument \(D\), and \(c_3=1\).  Choose fixed \(c_2>0\) and then \(c_1>0\) sufficiently small that
\[
 \frac{cc_1}{c_2^2}\le1,
 \qquad
 3c_2\log\!\left(\frac{3c_2}{2ec_1}\right)\ge2.
\tag{5}
\]
This is possible because the logarithm in (5) tends to infinity as \(c_1\downarrow0\).  Let \(\nu_0,\nu_1\) be the resulting distributions, orient their labels so that
\[
 h_1-h_0\ge \frac{c_4}{N\log N},
 \qquad h_j=E_{\nu_j}[p\mu],
\tag{6}
\]
and write
\[
 b=\frac{c_1\log N}{N},\qquad
 q=\frac{c_4D}{N\log N},\qquad
 \delta=4b\sqrt D.
\tag{7}
\]
Under hypothesis \(j\), draw \((p_k,\pi_k,\mu_k)\), \(1\le k\le D\), independently from \(\nu_j\).  The common first moment
\[
 a_0=E_{\nu_0}[p]=E_{\nu_1}[p]\le D^{-1}
\tag{8}
\]
allows us to append a residual coordinate
\[
 p_d=1-Da_0\ge0,\qquad \pi_d=\epsilon,\qquad \mu_d=0.
\tag{9}
\]
Define the conditioning event
\[
 E_j=
 \left\{\left|\sum_{k=1}^D p_k-Da_0\right|\le\delta,
 \ \left|\sum_{k=1}^D p_k\mu_k-Dh_j\right|\le\frac q4\right\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Independence, \(0\le p\le b\), and \(0\le p\mu\le b\) give
\[
 E_{\nu_j^{\otimes D}}
 \left[\left\{\sum_{k=1}^D(p_k-a_0)\right\}^2\right]
 =D\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_j}(p)\le Db^2
\tag{11}
\]
and
\[
 E_{\nu_j^{\otimes D}}
 \left[\left\{\sum_{k=1}^D(p_k\mu_k-h_j)\right\}^2\right]
 =D\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_j}(p\mu)\le Db^2.
\tag{12}
\]
For any centered random variable \(Z\), the pointwise inequality
\(t^2\mathbf 1\{|Z|>t\}\le Z^2\) yields
\(P(|Z|>t)\le E[Z^2]/t^2\).  Applying it to (11)--(12), then using (7), gives
\[
 P_j(E_j^c)
 \le \frac{Db^2}{\delta^2}
      +\frac{16Db^2}{q^2}
 \le \frac1{16}
      +\frac{16c_1^2\log^4N}{c_4^2D}.
\tag{13}
\]

We now derive the count-mixture distance rather than importing a squared-risk conclusion.  In one nonresidual cell, let
\[
 Z_k=(Z_{k11},Z_{k10},Z_{k0})
\tag{14}
\]
have conditionally independent coordinates with means
\[
 Np\pi\mu,\qquad Np\pi(1-\mu),\qquad Np(1-\pi),
\tag{15}
\]
respectively.  For nonnegative integers \(x,y,z\), its mixture probability under \(\nu_j\) is
\[
 E_{\nu_j}\!\left[
 e^{-Np}
 \frac{(Np\pi\mu)^x\{Np\pi(1-\mu)\}^y\{Np(1-\pi)\}^z}
 {x!y!z!}
 \right].
\tag{16}
\]
Expand \(e^{-Np}=\sum_{t\ge0}(-Np)^t/t!\).  The absolute series is summable because \(Np\le c_1\log N\).  Moreover,
\[
 p^t(p\pi\mu)^x\{p\pi(1-\mu)\}^y\{p(1-\pi)\}^z
\tag{17}
\]
is a polynomial of total degree \(t+x+y+z\) in the three coordinates
\[
 p,\qquad p\pi,\qquad p\pi\mu,
\tag{18}
\]
because \(p\pi(1-\mu)=p\pi-p\pi\mu\) and
\(p(1-\pi)=p-p\pi\).  Hence all terms of degree at most \(3K\), where \(K=c_2\log N\), cancel between the two mixture probabilities by the moment identities in \(\texttt{lem:zeng-moment-matching-triples}\).

For either prior, the sum of the absolute remaining terms over all \(x,y,z,t\) with \(x+y+z+t>3K\) is at most
\[
 \sum_{r>3K}\frac{(2c_1\log N)^r}{r!}
 =N^{2c_1}P\{W>3K\},
 \qquad W\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(2c_1\log N).
\tag{19}
\]
To verify the tail bound used in (19), if \(W\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda)\) and \(L>e\lambda\), exponential Markov with \(t=\log(L/\lambda)>1\) gives
\[
 P(W>L)
 \le \exp\{\lambda(e^t-1)-tL\}
 =e^{-\lambda}\left(\frac{e\lambda}{L}\right)^L.
\tag{20}
\]
Taking \(\lambda=2c_1\log N\), \(L=3c_2\log N\), and using (5), equations (19)--(20) give
\[
 \sum_{r>3K}\frac{(2c_1\log N)^r}{r!}
 \le
 \left(\frac{2ec_1}{3c_2}\right)^{3c_2\log N}
 \le N^{-2}.
\tag{21}
\]
The total-variation distance is one half the \(\ell^1\) distance of the mixture mass functions.  Equations (16)--(21), applied to both priors, therefore imply
\[
 \|\mathcal L_0(Z_k)-\mathcal L_1(Z_k)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le N^{-2}.
\tag{22}
\]
The \(D\) triples in (14) are independent before conditioning, and the residual-cell count has the same law under both hypotheses.  A telescoping expansion of the two product mass functions, followed by the triangle inequality, thus yields
\[
 \|\mathcal L_0(Z)-\mathcal L_1(Z)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le \sum_{k=1}^D
 \|\mathcal L_0(Z_k)-\mathcal L_1(Z_k)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le \frac{D}{N^2}
 \le \frac{\log N}{N},
\tag{23}
\]
where the last step uses (4).

Conditioning a probability measure \(\Gamma\) on an event \(E\) changes it in total variation by exactly \(\Gamma(E^c)\); applying a common observation kernel cannot increase total variation.  Consequently (13) and (23) imply that the two predictive count laws \(\widetilde Q_0,\widetilde Q_1\), after conditioning their parameter priors on \(E_0,E_1\), satisfy
\[
 \|\widetilde Q_0-\widetilde Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le \frac18
 +\frac{32c_1^2\log^4N}{c_4^2D}
 +\frac{\log N}{N}.
\tag{24}
\]
Choose \(A\) and then \(N_0\) large enough that, whenever
\(D\ge A\log^4N\) and \(N\ge N_0\), the last two terms in (24) are at most \(1/8\).  Then
\[
 \|\widetilde Q_0-\widetilde Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\frac14.
\tag{25}
\]

The relaxed one-arm targets are
\[
 \vartheta=M\sum_{k=1}^D p_k\mu_k.
\tag{26}
\]
Under the prior conditioned on \(E_j\), they lie in
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal T}_j
 =\left[M\left(Dh_j-\frac q4\right),
         M\left(Dh_j+\frac q4\right)\right].
\tag{27}
\]
Equations (6)--(7) give the direct separation
\[
 \Delta(\widetilde{\mathcal T}_0,\widetilde{\mathcal T}_1)
 \ge M\{D(h_1-h_0)-q/2\}
 \ge \frac{Mq}{2}.
\tag{28}
\]
Also, after (9), the total unnormalized mass \(S\) obeys on \(E_j\)
\[
 S=p_d+\sum_{k=1}^D p_k,
 \qquad |S-1|\le\delta.
\tag{29}
\]
Increasing \(N_0\) if necessary, (4) and (7) ensure
\[
 \delta\le4c_1\frac{\log^{3/2}N}{\sqrt N}\le\frac13.
\tag{30}
\]

It remains to connect this relaxed experiment to the exact class defining \(\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\).  Fix a parameter vector in either conditioned prior and normalize its cell masses to
\[
 p_k^\circ=p_k/S,\qquad 1\le k\le d.
\tag{31}
\]
Construct a full-data law \(P^\circ\) as follows: given \(X=k\), draw
\(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_k)\), set \(Y(0)=0\), draw
\(Y(1)=M B_k\) with \(B_k\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_k)\) independently of \(A\) conditional on \(X\), and set \(Y=Y(A)\).  Consistency and conditional exchangeability hold by construction.  The cited support gives fixed overlap.  Furthermore,
\[
 |E[Y\mid A=1,X=k]|=M\mu_k\le M,
 \qquad E[Y\mid A=0,X=k]=0,
\tag{32}
\]
and, for the treated arm,
\[
 E[(Y-M\mu_k)^4\mid A=1,X=k]
 =M^4E[(B_k-\mu_k)^4]
 \le M^4,
\tag{33}
\]
while the control-arm central fourth moment is zero.  Thus (31)--(33) and
\(\texttt{def:global-law-class}\) show
\[
 P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}.
\tag{34}
\]
By \(\texttt{def:ate-functional}\),
\[
 \tau(P^\circ)=\frac{M\sum_{k=1}^Dp_k\mu_k}{S}
 =\frac{\vartheta}{S}.
\tag{35}
\]
Since \(0\le\sum p_k\mu_k\le S\), equations (29) and (35) yield
\[
 |\tau(P^\circ)-\vartheta|
 =M\left(\sum_{k=1}^Dp_k\mu_k\right)
   \frac{|1-S|}{S}
 \le M|1-S|\le M\delta.
\tag{36}
\]

Under the Poisson experiment, let \(R\) be the total count over all cells and all three observable labels.  Conditional on the parameter,
\[
 R\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(NS),
\tag{37}
\]
and, conditional on \(R=r\), a parameter-free uniform ordering of the \(r\) observed labels is an iid sample from the observed margin of \(P^\circ\).  Attach such an ordering to the count statistic; because this is a common Markov kernel, (25) remains valid for the augmented experiment.

Let
\[
 L(C_n)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|C_n|].
\tag{38}
\]
Define an interval in the augmented Poisson experiment by
\[
 \widetilde C=
 \begin{cases}
 C_n(O_1^*,\ldots,O_n^*)+[-M\delta,M\delta],&R\ge n,\\
 [-2M,2M],&R<n,
 \end{cases}
\tag{39}
\]
where \(O_1^*,\ldots,O_n^*\) are the first \(n\) observations in the attached uniform ordering and \(+\) is Minkowski addition.  Conditional on every \(R=r\ge n\), these \(n\) observations have law \(Q_{P^\circ}^{(n)}\).  Hence admissibility of \(C_n\), (34), and (36) show pointwise for every relaxed parameter satisfying (29) that
\[
 P\{\vartheta\in\widetilde C\mid R=r\}\ge1-\alpha,
 \qquad r\ge n.
\tag{40}
\]
When \(R<n\), equations (26), (29), and (30) give
\(0\le\vartheta\le M(1+\delta)<2M\), so the second branch of (39) covers surely.  Thus
\[
 P\{\vartheta\in\widetilde C\}\ge1-\alpha
\tag{41}
\]
for every parameter in either conditioned relaxed prior.

The lower tail in (37) is exponentially small.  Indeed, with
\(\lambda=NS\ge(2/3)N=8n/3\), one has \(n\le\lambda/2\); exponential Markov at \(t=\log2\) gives
\[
 P\{\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda)\le\lambda/2\}
 \le \exp\{\lambda((\log2)/2-1/2)\}
 \le e^{-\lambda/8}\le e^{-n/3}.
\tag{42}
\]
For every \(r\ge n\), (34), (38), and the conditional iid property imply that the conditional expected length of the first interval in (39), before enlargement, is at most \(L(C_n)\).  Therefore
\[
 E[|\widetilde C|]
 \le L(C_n)+2M\delta+4Me^{-n/3}
\tag{43}
\]
under either conditioned prior-predictive law.

For completeness, we apply coverage to length directly in this augmented experiment.  Let
\(G_j=\{\widetilde C\cap\widetilde{\mathcal T}_j\ne\varnothing\}\).  Equation (41) and prior support on (27) give
\[
 \widetilde Q_j(G_j)\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{44}
\]
By (25),
\[
 \widetilde Q_0(G_1)
 \ge\widetilde Q_1(G_1)
   -\|\widetilde Q_0-\widetilde Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \ge1-\alpha-\frac14.
\tag{45}
\]
The union bound, (44), and (45) yield
\[
 \widetilde Q_0(G_0\cap G_1)
 \ge1-2\alpha-\frac14>\frac14,
\tag{46}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(\alpha<1/4\).  On \(G_0\cap G_1\), the interval has length at least the separation in (28).  Thus
\[
 E_{\widetilde Q_0}[|\widetilde C|]
 \ge \frac{Mq}{2}\left(1-2\alpha-\frac14\right)
 \ge\frac{Mq}{8}.
\tag{47}
\]
Combining (43) and (47) gives
\[
 L(C_n)\ge\frac{Mq}{8}-2M\delta-4Me^{-n/3}.
\tag{48}
\]

Finally choose \(A\) still larger, if necessary, so that
\[
 D\ge A\log^4N
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \frac{2\delta}{q}
 =\frac{8c_1\log^2N}{c_4\sqrt D}\le\frac1{32},
\tag{49}
\]
and increase \(N_0\) so that \(4e^{-n/3}\le q/32\) throughout this regime.  The latter is possible because (7) and \(D\ge A\log^4N\) imply
\(q\ge c_4A\log^3N/N\), whereas \(N=4n\).  Equations (48)--(49) then prove
\[
 L(C_n)\ge\frac{Mq}{16}
 \ge c_\epsilon M\frac{d}{n\log(en)}.
\tag{50}
\]
For the second inequality, use \(D=d-1\ge d/2\) in the present regime,
\(N=4n\), and \(\log N\le(\log4)\log(en)\).

It remains only to check the complementary ranges.  If \(N<N_0\), then
\(d/[n\log(en)]\le1\le C_{N_0}n^{-1/2}\).  If
\(D<A\log^4N\), then
\[
 \frac{d}{n\log(en)}
 \le C_A\frac{1+\log^3(en)}{n}
 \le C_A' n^{-1/2}.
\tag{51}
\]
The last inequality is uniform because
\(\log(en)=1+\log n\le(1+6/e)n^{1/6}\), the latter following by maximizing
\((\log x)x^{-1/6}\) over \(x\ge1\).  Thus (2) also dominates the rare-cell term in every range not covered by (50).

Equations (2), (50), and (51) show, for all
\(d\le c_\epsilon n\log(en)\),
\[
 \mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}
 \ge c_{\epsilon,\alpha}M
 \max\!\left\{n^{-1/2},\frac{d}{n\log(en)}\right\}
 \ge \frac{c_{\epsilon,\alpha}M}{2}
 \min\!\left\{1,n^{-1/2}+\frac{d}{n\log(en)}\right\}.
\tag{52}
\]
The final expression is a constant multiple of \(r_{n,d,M}\) by
\(\texttt{def:frontier-scale}\), which proves the claim.

statements.proof_tex:
By \(thm:global\text{-}honest\text{-}upper\), the particular measurable
interval \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\) is admissible in the infimum defining
\(\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}
 \le \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]
 \le C_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}.
\tag{1}
\]
Conversely, \(thm:same\text{-}class\text{-}testing\text{-}converse\) applies
to every interval admitted by \(def:minimax\text{-}honest\text{-}length\), so
taking first its supremum over \(P\) and then the infimum over intervals gives
\[
 \mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}
 \ge c_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}.
\tag{2}
\]
Substitution of \(def:frontier\text{-}scale\) into (1)--(2) proves the displayed
equivalence uniformly on \(d\le c_\epsilon n\log(en)\).  Finally,
\(prop:certified\text{-}finite\text{-}precision\text{-}implementation\) gives
coverage of the outward-rounded interval and adds at most
\(2\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\le2r_{n,d,M}\) to its expected length.  Thus it has
the same constant-order upper bound.

statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in
\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\), and suppress the row subscript on
\(p_k,\pi_k,\mu_{ak}\).  All constants below may depend on
\(\epsilon,c_0,K_0\), but not on \(n,d_n\), or the chosen member of the
triangular class.  Membership in \(def:balanced\text{-}local\text{-}class\)
gives, separately, iid sampling, fixed overlap, the cell-mean envelope, the
conditional fourth-central-moment envelope, the lower cell-mass bound,
\(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), and
\[
 v_0M^2\le V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\le v_1M^2.
\tag{1}
\]

First derive the nuisance rates rather than assuming them.  For a validation
fold \(I_s\), write \(m_s=n-|I_s|\) for its training size.  Since \(K_0\) is
fixed and the fold sizes differ by at most one, \(m_s\ge c_Kn\) for a constant
\(c_K>0\).  Let \(N_{ak,-s}\) and \(N_{k,-s}\) be the corresponding training
arm-cell and cell counts.  Cauchy--Schwarz and
\(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\) give
\[
 E_{P_n}[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid X=k,A=a]
 \le
 \{E_{P_n}[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid X=k,A=a]\}^{1/2}
 \le M^2.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\), direct integration of the binomial
probability generating function gives
\[
 E[(N+1)^{-1}]=\frac{1-(1-q)^{m+1}}{(m+1)q},
 \qquad
 N^{-1}\mathbf1\{N>0\}\le2(N+1)^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
Conditionally on \(N_{ak,-s}=r>0\), the fitted cell mean is the average of
\(r\) observations from the conditional arm-cell law.  By (2), its conditional
mean-squared error is at most \(M^2/r\).  When \(r=0\), the zero fallback in
\(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\) has squared error at most \(M^2\) by
\(ass:cell\text{-}mean\text{-}envelope\).  With
\(q_{ak}=P_n(X=k,A=a)\ge\epsilon p_k\), equations (2)--(3) therefore imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E\!\left[\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
  (\widehat\mu_{ak}^{(-s)}-\mu_{ak})^2\right]
 &\le M^2\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 \left\{e^{-m_sq_{ak}}+\frac{2}{(m_s+1)q_{ak}}\right\}\\
 &\le C_\epsilon M^2
 \left\{e^{-c_\epsilon m_s/d_n}+\frac{d_n}{m_s}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
The last inequality uses \(p_k\ge c_0/d_n\) and
\(\sum_kp_k=1\).  For the propensity estimate, condition on
\(N_{k,-s}\).  On a nonempty cell its unprojected empirical proportion has
conditional variance at most \(1/(4N_{k,-s})\); on an empty cell its squared
error is at most one.  Projection on
\([\epsilon/2,1-\epsilon/2]\) cannot increase distance from
\(\pi_k\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\).  Repeating (3) gives
\[
 E\!\left[\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
  (\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_k)^2\right]
 \le C\left\{e^{-c m_s/d_n}+\frac{d_n}{m_s}\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Because \(n/d_n\to\infty\), the exponential terms are smaller than any
inverse power of \(n\).  Markov's inequality applied to (4)--(5), for each of
the fixed number of folds, yields
\[
 \|\widehat\mu_a^{(-s)}-\mu_a\|_{P_n,2}
   =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M\sqrt{d_n/n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\pi^{(-s)}-\pi\|_{P_n,2}
   =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(\sqrt{d_n/n}).
\tag{6}
\]

Define the uncentered augmented score
\[
 g(O;\eta)=m_1(X)-m_0(X)
 +\frac{A\{Y-m_1(X)\}}{e(X)}
 -\frac{(1-A)\{Y-m_0(X)\}}{1-e(X)},
\tag{7}
\]
where \(\eta=(e,m_0,m_1)\), and let
\(\eta_0=(\pi,\mu_0,\mu_1)\).  The definitions of the conditional means,
fixed overlap, and \(def:ate\text{-}functional\) give
\[
 E_{P_n}[g(O;\eta_0)]=\tau(P_n),
 \qquad g(O;\eta_0)-\tau(P_n)=\phi_{P_n}(O).
\tag{8}
\]
For the nuisance estimate trained outside fold \(s\), put
\(D_s(O)=g(O;\widehat\eta^{(-s)})-g(O;\eta_0)\).  Conditioning on the
training sample and evaluating (7) within each cell gives the exact
orthogonality remainder
\[
 P_nD_s=\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 (\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_k)
 \left\{
 \frac{\widehat\mu_{1k}^{(-s)}-\mu_{1k}}
      {\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 +\frac{\widehat\mu_{0k}^{(-s)}-\mu_{0k}}
      {1-\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 \right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Every denominator in (9) is at least \(\epsilon/2\).  Cauchy--Schwarz and
(6) therefore show
\[
 |P_nD_s|=O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(Md_n/n)
          =o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(Mn^{-1/2}),
\tag{10}
\]
where the last equality uses \(ass:local\text{-}dimension\).

The same score algebra, \(|\widehat\pi-\pi|\le1\), the clipped denominators,
and (2) imply the conditional second-moment bound
\[
 P_nD_s^2\le C_\epsilon\left[
 \sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 (\widehat\mu_{ak}^{(-s)}-\mu_{ak})^2
 +M^2\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 (\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_k)^2\right]
 =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M^2d_n/n).
\tag{11}
\]
Conditionally on the training data, observations in \(I_s\) are independent
of \(\widehat\eta^{(-s)}\).  Hence
\[
 (\mathbb P_{I_s}-P_n)D_s
 =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M\sqrt{d_n}/n).
\tag{12}
\]
Summing (9)--(12) over the fixed number of folds, with weights
\(|I_s|/n\), and using the definition of \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)
 &=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{g(O_i;\eta_0)-\tau(P_n)\}
   +O_P(Md_n/n)+O_P(M\sqrt{d_n}/n)\\
 &=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)
   +o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
Here and below the final little-oh is under \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\); \(M\) is the
fixed scale indexing the class.

It remains to verify the variance statement.  From
\(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\), \(|\tau(P_n)|\le2M\), fixed overlap, and
\(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\), the inequality
\(|x_1+x_2+x_3|^4\le27\sum_{j=1}^3|x_j|^4\) applied to
\(def:efficient\text{-}influence\text{-}function\) yields
\[
 E_{P_n}|\phi_{P_n}(O)|^4\le C_\epsilon M^4.
\tag{14}
\]
Consequently Chebyshev's inequality, (1), and (14) give
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)^2
   -V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)=o_P(M^2),
 \qquad
 \overline\phi_n^2=o_P(M^2).
\tag{15}
\]
Furthermore, conditioning fold by fold in (11) and applying Markov's
inequality gives
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{s=0}^{K_0-1}\sum_{i\in I_s}D_s(O_i)^2
 =O_P(M^2d_n/n)=o_P(M^2).
\tag{16}
\]
Writing the fitted score as
\(\widehat\psi_i=\tau(P_n)+\phi_{P_n}(O_i)+D_s(O_i)\) for
\(i\in I_s\), the elementary inequality
\[
 \left|\frac1n\sum_i(u_i+v_i-\overline u-\overline v)^2
       -\frac1n\sum_i(u_i-\overline u)^2\right|
 \le2\left\{\frac1n\sum_i(u_i-\overline u)^2
             \frac1n\sum_i(v_i-\overline v)^2\right\}^{1/2}
      +\frac1n\sum_i(v_i-\overline v)^2
\tag{17}
\]
with \(u_i=\phi_{P_n}(O_i)\), \(v_i=D_s(O_i)\), together with
(15)--(16), proves
\[
 \widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)=o_P(M^2).
\tag{18}
\]
Division in (18) is legitimate by the lower bound in (1), and proves
\(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\to1\).

Finally, (1) and (14) imply
\[
 \sup_n\frac{E_{P_n}|\phi_{P_n}(O)|^4}
                 {V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)^2}
 \le C_\epsilon/v_0^2<\infty.
\tag{19}
\]
The mean-zero identity required by
\(lem:order\text{-}one\text{-}self\text{-}normalized\text{-}clt\) is (8),
and iid sampling and positive variance are supplied by
\(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\) and (1).  That cited order-one result and (19)
therefore give
\[
 \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)}
 {\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n[\phi_{P_n}(O_i)-\overline\phi_n]^2\right\}^{1/2}}
 \Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{20}
\]
By (15), the denominator in (20), divided by
\(\sqrt{nV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}\), converges in probability to one.  For any
\(x\in\mathbb R\) and \(0<\delta<1\), intersecting with the event that this
ratio lies in \([1-\delta,1+\delta]\) sandwiches the distribution function of
the oracle standardized mean between the distribution functions in (20) at
the smaller and larger of \(x/(1-\delta)\) and \(x/(1+\delta)\), up to a
probability tending to zero.
First let \(n\to\infty\) and then \(\delta\downarrow0\); continuity of the
standard-normal distribution function proves
\[
 \frac{1}{\sqrt{nV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}}
 \sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{21}
\]
Combining (13), (21), and the lower variance bound in (1) proves the final
displayed normal limit and completes the proof of the narrowed theorem.
